column1: # note: <tool>_ms = COLD full-file CLI check from scratch. Only basilisk and mypy have a -warm column (they keep a real cross-run cache): basilisk-warm = --cache result-cache hit; mypy-warm = incremental .mypy_cache hit (cold mypy = --no-incremental). pyright/ty/pyrefly/zuban keep NO cross-run result cache (a repeat run = cold)
column2: so they are measured cold-only. mypy runs with --strict so it performs the strict-mode analysis the fixtures stress (plain mypy reports 'no issues' on the strictness fixtures); zuban runs as `zuban mypy --strict` for the same reason (its default `zuban check` mode skips these strictness rules).
